title: RS11 Benchmark Results Summary
paper: Santos RL, Coutinho-Almeida J, Cruz-Correia RJ. A Database-First Architecture for Trustworthy Medical Vocabulary Validation with Small Language Models: An AI-Assisted Evidence Synthesis with Supplementary Empirical Evaluation.
status: Manuscript to be submitted to the International Journal of Medical Informatics (prior submission reference: IJMEDI-D-26-01592)
scheme_note: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE: the manuscript supplement (Table S11 and note S11.1) is authoritative for configuration letters, case counts and mechanisms. This file gives the five phases of the two archived 14-case runs of benchmark_3phase_rag.py whose phase 4 is Configuration J, and phase 4 of Configurations K, L and M, each with its result file; the result files are available on request (supplement S11). Configurations H, J, K and L were run with earlier versions of the script in this folder, and the two phase-4 runs of Configuration M with a harness that is not archived (supplement S11). Until 2026-10-06 this file listed a package series A-M whose stages B-I no archived run reproduces; that series was replaced.
hardware: Apple M1 MacBook Pro (MacBookPro17,1), 16GB unified memory, macOS Darwin 25.3.0

chromadb_collections.note: Collections in the authors' local ChromaDB store; benchmark_3phase_rag.py reads only icd10cm_terminology. Counts at the time of the March 2026 runs were not recorded.

phases.phase2: + verification of the answer against the database
phases.phase4: The six approaches of supplement S11, including the abbreviation dictionary (Configuration J)

runs_14_cases.note: Table S11 gives both files for Configuration J (14/14 in both); the path partition of the 14 cases is that of phase 4 of the 20 March file: 8 by the confidence-gated database path, 6 by model-mediated paths (supplement S11, S17.5). Table S11 reports Configuration H as phase 3 of an earlier run (benchmark_3phase_rag_20260320_110529.json, 10/14).

configs_42_cases.name: Expanded dictionary; ICD-10-PCS routed to Vocab2; ICD-11 import
Cross-encoder re-ranker (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2), in the run that preceded K on the same day
configs_42_cases.note: 28/42 in the preceding run without the re-ranker (benchmark_3phase_rag_20260323_154902.json, phase 4); E-LOINC-01 and E-LOINC-03 lost, none gained (supplement S11)

configs_42_cases.name: 94-entry abbreviation dictionary, in a harness that is not archived
configs_42_cases.note: Both result files hold phase 4 only (30/42 each), with the keys config (M) and dict_size (94), and no committed version of benchmark_3phase_rag.py writes dict_size; the script in this folder is the version committed after these runs, with a security patch of 11 August 2026 (supplement S11)

key_findings: Phase 0 (no retrieval): 6/14 (42.9%) and 5/14 in the two runs whose phase 4 is Configuration J
Phases 1-3 (database candidates, verification, vocabulary routing): 9-10/14 (64.3-71.4%) in the same two runs

Phase 4 (Configuration J): 14/14 in both runs; in the 20 March run, 8 of the 14 by the confidence-gated database path and 6 by model-mediated paths, 3 of them with an ICD-10-CM code the model emitted from memory, one never confirmed in the database (supplement S11, S17.5)

A general-purpose cross-encoder re-ranker (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) lowered accuracy from 28/42 to 26/42 (-4.8pp) in a single run; a cross-encoder trained on clinical query-code pairs was not tested (supplement S11)
Scoring: 1 of the 14 and 2 of the 42 cases are scored by a response-length threshold, and 2 further extended cases on a placeholder answer (supplement S11.1)

Re-runs: the two runs of Configuration J agree in phases 3 and 4 and differ in phases 0-2; the nine archived runs of the script on the 14 focused cases, made between 19 and 22 March 2026 while it was under development, recorded phase 3 at 57.1-78.6%; no invariance is claimed (supplement S11.1)
